title: Managing aged accounts receivable reports on Mac: a guide for medical billers
metaTitle: Managing aged accounts receivable reports on Mac: a guide for medical billers
description: Learn how to manage aged accounts receivable reports on your Mac. Discover causes for unpaid claims and manual fixes to improve your revenue cycle efficiency.
intro: Managing aged accounts receivable reports is the most critical task for keeping a medical practice solvent. You spend your day hunting down unpaid claims, yet the process often feels like a constant battle against automated denials.
tldr: Aged accounts receivable reports track claims that have gone unpaid past the standard 30 to 90 day window.
Most denials are preventable through front-end verification and better claim scrubbing before submission.
You can manage these reports effectively on a Mac using web-based practice management software and Excel.
Lazur helps by letting you dictate notes and look up information without leaving your billing software.

blocks.text: Why managing aged accounts receivable reports is difficult

When you open your aged accounts receivable report, you are looking at the health of the practice. A long list of claims over 90 days usually signals a breakdown in the revenue cycle. On a Mac, you likely access this through a web browser like Chrome or Safari. The data often exports to CSV or Excel formats. The challenge is not just the volume of claims, but the detective work required for each one.
Common causes for unpaid medical claims

items: Missing or incorrect patient insurance information entered at the front desk.
Expired authorizations that were not updated before the date of service.
Coding errors where the ICD-10 or CPT code does not match the clinical documentation.
Payer automation that rejects claims based on minor technicalities before a human sees them.
Lack of timely follow up after an initial denial is received.

blocks.text: Fixes for your follow up routine

You do not need expensive software to improve your follow up. Start by segmenting your report by payer. Focus on the oldest claims first to prevent write-offs. Use Excel to highlight claims that are hitting the 60 day mark. Set up a recurring task in your calendar to review these specific accounts every Tuesday and Thursday morning. When you call an insurance company, keep a log of the representative name, the reference number, and the date. This documentation is your best defense if the claim is denied a second time.
Using your Mac for better billing efficiency

Since you work on a Mac, you have the advantage of a stable Unix-based system. Use Spaces to keep your billing software on one desktop and your communication tools on another. Use ⌃ 1 through ⌃ 4 to switch between these spaces quickly. When you are on hold with an insurance provider, keep a blank document open to jot down notes. If you use Outlook for your email, create templates for common appeal letters. This saves you from typing the same information repeatedly.

faq.question: How often should I review my aged accounts receivable report?
faq.answer: You should review your report at least weekly. Prioritize claims based on dollar amount and age to ensure you are working on the accounts that impact the practice revenue the most.

faq.question: Can I use Excel on my Mac for tracking claims?
faq.answer: Yes, Excel for Mac is fully functional for tracking and sorting your aged accounts receivable reports. Use conditional formatting to highlight claims that are approaching 90 days.

costs.title: Labor expense
costs.text: Every minute spent on hold or investigating a denial is time taken away from submitting new claims.

costs.title: Revenue leakage
costs.text: Claims that are not followed up on eventually become uncollectible write-offs.

causes.title: Front-end errors
causes.text: Incorrect patient data entry remains the leading cause of initial claim denials.

causes.title: Payer complexity
causes.text: Frequent changes in insurance policies and automated denial rules make it harder to get claims paid on the first try.

fixes.title: Proactive verification
fixes.text: Verify insurance eligibility at least 48 hours before the patient appointment.

fixes.title: Standardized appeal process
fixes.text: Create a library of appeal letter templates to ensure all required information is included in your first appeal.

plan.label: Morning
plan.title: Review and prioritize
plan.text: Spend the first hour reviewing the aging report and identifying the top 10 claims by dollar value that need immediate attention.

plan.label: Mid-day
plan.title: Follow up calls
plan.text: Dedicate time to calling insurance providers for claims that have been pending for more than 30 days.

plan.title: Data entry and appeals
plan.text: Process new denials and draft appeals for claims that have clear documentation to support payment.
